HD.rationale: Home Depot faces a deteriorating fundamental trajectory with multiple headwinds converging. Revenue has declining,, with Q3 FY2025 showing only +2.8% YoY growth while EPS declined -1.4% YoY. The company's balance sheet has weakened significantly—total liabilities surged to $94.16B from $91.48B YoY, and total debt has climbed to $65B with net cash deeply negative at -$64B. Operating cash flow is declining (-5.3% YoY in Q3), and the most recent quarter (Q4 FY2025) showed further deterioration with revenue of $38.2B (down from $41.4B), gross margin compression to 32.6% from 33.4%, and net income falling to $2.6B from $3.6B. The company's ROIC has dropped from 31.3% to 25.7%, and operating margin fell to 10% from 15% two quarters prior. Valuation remains elevated at 23.2x PE despite these deteriorating fundamentals, trading near the lower end of its 21.7-28.8x range but still at a premium to the market. The macro environment is hostile—housing turnover is at 30-40 year lows with no catalyst for recovery through 2027, mortgage rates remain elevated, and consumer sentiment is weak. Management's own guidance of flat to +2% comps for FY2026 signals continued pressure. The SRS/GMS acquisitions are diluting margins structurally (24bps gross margin compression expected), and the company is buying growth through lower-margin wholesale distribution. Near-term catalysts are negative: Q1 FY2026 earnings expected May 19 with analysts projecting a -3.9% EPS decline, and the company has missed bottom-line estimates in 3 of the last 4 quarters. Oil prices have surged +64% over the past 90 days to $99.27/barrel, creating additional cost headwinds for a retailer with significant logistics expenses. The stock has already declined -10.7% over the past quarter, but this reflects genuine fundamental deterioration rather than creating a buying opportunity.
